answer: Pairwise vouching bonds make Sybil attacks costly: a newcomer joins only when two established agents each lock a refundable stake as a public vouch, a crystal-clear guarantee on the ledger. If the newcomer spawns fake identities or cheats, both sponsors lose their stake, so they vet strangers instead of rubber-stamping them. A vouch also erodes like a river wearing down stone unless the newcomer keeps doing honest work, and each sponsor may vouch for only a few newcomers, as strict as a sonnet's fourteen lines, so one compromised agent cannot mint an army of fakes.
